coverage_note: Licensed professional employees of local boards of education under the Professional Educators Collaborative Conferencing Act of 2011 (Tenn. Code Ann. 49-5-601 et seq.), as enacted by 2011 Pub. Acts ch. 378. Later amendments are not captured. No statute granting bargaining or conferencing rights to other Tennessee public employees was captured.

governing_statute.value: Professional Educators Collaborative Conferencing Act of 2011, Tenn. Code Ann. 49-5-601 et seq. (replaced the Education Professional Negotiations Act); text as enacted in 2011
governing_statute.quote: This part shall be known and may be cited as the "Professional Educators Collaborative Conferencing Act of 2011 ".
governing_statute.pinpoint: Tenn. Code Ann. 49-5-601(a), as enacted by 2011 Pub. Acts ch. 378, sec. 1

labor_board.null_reason: The 2011 Act creates no labor board: unlawful-act complaints go first to the board of education and then to chancery court (49-5-606(c)(1)), and conferencing representatives are chosen by a poll run by a special question committee.

ulp_limitation_period.value: Three months: no complaint may issue on an unlawful act that occurred more than three months before the complaint was filed
ulp_limitation_period.quote: (2) No complaint shall issue based upon any unlawful act occurring more than three (3) months prior to the filing of the complaint.

who_may_bargain.value: Licensed professional employees of local boards of education, excluding the management team (principals, assistant principals, supervisors and other administrators) and certain re-employed retired teachers. They confer, not bargain, through representatives chosen in a poll.
who_may_bargain.quote: (8) "Professional employee" means any person employed by any local board of education in a position that requires a license issued by the Department of Education for service in public elementary and secondary schools of this state

scope_of_bargaining.value: Collaborative conferencing limited to salaries or wages, grievance procedures, insurance, fringe benefits (not state retirement), working conditions not set by law, leave, and payroll deductions (as enacted in 2011); other subjects, including differentiated and incentive pay, are barred
scope_of_bargaining.quote: Such terms and conditions include and are limited to the following: (1) Salaries or wages; (2) Grievance procedures; (3) Insurance; (4) Fringe benefits, but not to include pensions or retirement programs of the Tennessee consolidated retirement system or locally authorized early retirement incentives;

impasse_procedure.value: None. Agreement is not required; absent a memorandum of understanding the board of education sets the terms by board policy
impasse_procedure.quote: Absent an agreement and memorandum of understanding on terms and conditions specified for collaborative conferencing in this act, the board of education shall have the authority to address such terms and conditions through board policy.

strike_legality.value: Prohibited: engaging in a strike is an unlawful act; strikes may be enjoined in chancery court and strikers may be dismissed and lose tenure
strike_legality.quote: (2) If the court finds, after a hearing, that a strike has occurred, the court shall enjoin the employees from participating in the strike.

notes: The official Tennessee Code is a script-only LexisNexis portal, and capitol.tn.gov and wapp.capitol.tn.gov robots.txt disallow all user agents. The Act was captured from the Secretary of State's publications host (publications.tnsosfiles.com), whose robots.txt request returns an S3 'AccessDenied' for a missing object (treated as no robots file under RFC 9309) when fetched with the short form of the lane's user agent; the long form is refused by a CloudFront rule.
All cells cite the 2011 session law; amendments after 2011 (for example to payroll deductions) are not reflected and should be checked against the current code.
